answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a bonded registry, then earn access only by completing randomly assigned jobs whose results are checked by several established agents. A hidden thread links each bond to its payment history, while a jetty of mutually audited agents can slash deposits when identities collude or equivocate. A walnut-sized fake cluster therefore gains little: the attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every identity and loses it when caught.
